I decided to overhaul my entire routine in January of this year, not as part of a resolution, but I had plateaued and frustrated with my lack of progress. I was following a typical bodybuilding routine, 5 days a week, 3 to 4 sets of 6-10 rep pyramids. I moved a strong lift to the front of each day, bench press, deadlift, sqaut, etc. and dropped my reps to 2-3 on that one exercise (2 minute rest). Everything else I do that day is a 5 targeted exercised, 5 sets of 8-10 reps incorporating some supersets. I blew through the plateau in about a month and a half.
I like this over a straight 5x5 routine.

I just started using it today after finding out about it this morning - it seems to be a cut-down version of Chrome/Opera (written by the guy who started Opera) using WebKit. The UI is one of the best I've seen in a browser for a long time because it doesn't relegate all the functions outside of webpages to one button like Chrome/Firefox do. It also doesn't bother with the traditional window frame, instead using a "borderless window" model - something I wish Chrome/Firefox had started doing long ago, because they no longer fit with the style of the window frame.

Overall I give it 9/10 - I don't like Webkit's developer toolbox (I've always liked Firefox's toolbox).
